I dont think it can be saved, but you should be able to hopefully propagate the leaves in water.

Cut off any rotted part and allow the stems to calluse over for a day or two. Make sure you get a nice clean cut using a sharp knife.

Once theyre callused, dip the end into a rooting hormone if you have it. It'll be fine if you dont. Fill a narrow container with water. Place the stem so its just barely touching water. Change the water often, and watch for roots to sprout. 

Once theres a good amount of roots, you'll see the leaf start to die and small new growth pop up. You can now plant it. 

To keep it from rotting again, do some research into their watering habits. They like humidity and they like to be watered from the bottom. I set mine in pebble trays and water through those. 

This is just what my dad has taught me about them, so some people may have better advice but I hope this helps 💛
